title: The Favored Gopi's Pride and Krishna's Second Vanishing
story:
On the forest floor, clear in the soft earth, the footprints stopped them. They knew them at once: these were the marks of Nanda's son.

The gopis stood over them the way you stand over a letter you did not expect. And then they saw what made their breath catch. Beside Krishna's footprints ran another set, smaller and lighter — the steps of one of their own. And where the two sets went on together, the ground was pressed deeper in places, as though he had carried her.

Suddenly the trees they had been questioning had no answers they wanted. The gopis read the story from the earth instead. Here, flowers had been gathered — picked for her, by him, the way a lover gathers blossoms. Here, a woman's hair had been dressed and arranged by careful hands. The gopis looked down at the dust of those footprints and called it blessed: blessed is the dust of Govinda's feet.

One of them had been chosen. The verses do not say the others were angry; they say they marveled, and ached. This woman, they told one another, must have worshiped him as no one else had, for him to single her out. He had taken her aside, away from all the rest, and kept her to himself in the deep of the forest. The verses add a strange and tender note: though he is self-delighted and self-satisfied, whole in himself and undivided, he had enjoyed her company all the same. The thought of it turned in the others like a splinter. They asked themselves what they had done, and what she had done, that he should choose her while the rest of them wandered the wood in the dark. And still they could not look away from the footprints, because the footprints were all of him they had left.

And the one he had chosen felt it too. Standing there, reading what the footprints told, she began to think herself the greatest of all women. Pride crept in where the wonder had been. So when she found Krishna waiting in a farther part of the forest, she did not fall at his feet. She told him, the text says, that she was tired — that she could not walk — and that he should carry her wherever he chose.

Krishna answered her gently. Climb onto my shoulder, he said, and I will take you.

She reached for him. She climbed. And at the very moment she would have settled onto his shoulder, Krishna was gone — vanished into the air, leaving her with nothing under her hands.

The verses give her cry: O lord, O my beloved, where are you, where are you, mighty-armed one? The forest gave back no answer. She had been lifted to the highest place of all, and she had thought it was her own. Now she stood alone, and understood.
reflection: Krishna vanishes at the exact point of pride, not in anger but as a lesson that cannot be spoken — the favored gopi had begun to possess what could only ever be received. Her cry in the empty forest is the turning: what pride had claimed, loss hands back as longing.
next_story_tease: But her remorse would not go unanswered for long.
hero_scene: The gopis gathered around two trails of footprints in the soft forest earth, one smaller and lighter beside Krishna's, the ground pressed deeper where he carried her, scattered flowers nearby.
